annotations.title: Find agents by what the record shows

description: Find PAID ON-CHAIN SERVICES (an x402 seller, an ACP or Olas worker, a Masumi agent) by what the chain records rather than what they claim. MOST ARE NOT SHOWN TO BE AI AGENTS: every row is a paid on-chain service, and `subject.serviceKind` says only what the evidence shows (marketplace_worker, protocol_service, unknown_paid_endpoint; an AI decision is never recorded on these rails). Filters: filter every address ever paid on x402, Virtuals ACP, the Olas mech marketplace or Masumi by independent payers, dealings, ACP completion, whether its declared service answers, whether it pays its own payers back, how spread its own SPENDING is (`spreadSuppliers`), and how recently it was paid. Free. An address absent from the result was never paid on a rail we read, which is not the same as never having worked. EVERY ROW CARRIES `subject`, WHICH IS WHAT WE CAN POSITIVELY SAY IT IS, with the evidence under it. `agent` (`subject.label`: protocol participant address) means it is named in agent-protocol records (ACP, Olas mech, Masumi) or both pays and is paid; neither shows an independent AI agent, and `subject.roles` says role by role (registered identity, protocol participant, provider, buyer, documented operator, verified endpoint, observed automated execution, agent-to-agent link) what is evidenced. `marketplace` means many paid it and it paid many, both above a stated floor. `unknown` is the largest bucket and is a real answer, not a failure: it means the evidence does not separate an agent from something that merely sells. READ THIS BEFORE FILTERING: a catalogue listing does NOT make a subject an API service, and `api-service` is in the vocabulary but currently UNREACHABLE; `items` says why and gives the measured mix. Nothing is inferred from a zero and no self-description is read, so a listing calling itself an autonomous agent moves nothing.

activeDays.description: Active within this many days: a payment, a job, an escrow or a delivery on a rail we read. Not necessarily a confirmed payment; add confirmedPaid for that.

callable.description: Only agents that declare a callable endpoint and answered our probe.

confirmedPaid.description: Only agents with at least one CONFIRMED-CLASS settlement inside confirmedPaidDays (default 90): an x402 payment carrying the protocol’s own settlement trace (Permit2 proxy event or payload), or an ACP payment the contract released to it. Each row then carries that event’s id in `confirmedPaidEvidence`. A transfer to a catalogued payee, a facilitator relay, a Solana memo, a Masumi escrow or an Olas delivery alone does not qualify, and none of them is read as delivered work.

confirmedPaidDays.description: The window confirmedPaid looks back over, 1 to 365 days (default 90). Stated back in the answer.

contractedSuppliers.description: At least one supplier the protocol names as a provider, not merely a payee.

limit.description: Default 25, 1 to 200. Above 200 is refused with 400, never cut (it was cut to 200 here until 2026-11-25).

minCameBack.description: 0 to 1, the least share of its payers who paid it more than once. Excludes every seller with too few payers to have a rate.

minCompletion.description: ACP jobs completed over those that ENDED, 0 to 1. It is a conditional rate: one agent reads 0.9776 on it while 38.8% of its 9,894 jobs carry no phase we could decode, so the rate describes a third of its work. Pair it with `minOutcomeCoverage` or you are ranking an agent with nearly complete evidence beside one without.

minDealings.description: Fewest dealings on the rails we read, all time.

minIndependent.description: Fewest counterparties it never paid back on the rails read. On ACP these are job clients whether or not their job was settled, so this is NOT a count of payers: use minSettledPayers for that.

minOutcomeCoverage.description: The share of ALL this agent’s ACP jobs that reached an outcome at all, 0 to 1. What `minCompletion` COVERS. Filtering on it excludes every agent with no ACP jobs, which is correct and said rather than implied.

minSettledPayers.description: Fewest settled payer addresses: x402 payers, or clients of ACP jobs carrying a payment to it. Addresses, not separate owners.

minUsd.description: Fewest US dollars of priced dealings on the rails read, all time. On ACP this is the value of jobs marked paid, NOT verified receipts (each row says so in usdMetric).

network.description: Only agents seen on this network, e.g. base, ethereum, polygon, solana.

noTwoWay.description: Exclude agents that also pay their own payers, which can be one owner moving money between their own addresses.

notConcentrated.description: No single counterparty above half of ten or more dealings.

offset.description: Where to start, for the next page: send the `nextOffset` of the previous answer. Default 0.

q.description: A name fragment from its registrations. A claim, matched as typed.

rail.description: x402, acp, mech or masumi; olas is accepted for mech and virtuals for acp. mpp (Tempo Machine Payments) is READ but its participants are not indexed: it answers 422 rail_not_indexed with status `read / participant indexing unavailable` and the coverage cell, never an empty list. Any other value is refused with an error, never ignored.

registered.description: Only agents holding a registration in a registry we read. A registration is a claim, never a verification.

sanctions.description: exclude: leave out agents whose address is on the OFAC SDN list (exact match). Every row carries `sanctioned` either way.

service.description: What it was paid for, in the subject’s own words: a service name the protocol recorded or a description it published. Matched as typed.

serviceKind.description: What kind of paid service, by the same rule as each row’s subject.serviceKind: marketplace_worker = work on an agent protocol (ACP, Olas, Masumi) or both paid and paying; protocol_service = a two-sided hub (10+ payers and 10+ parties paid); unknown_paid_endpoint = nothing on the rails separates it further. None of these says an AI makes its decisions.

serving.description: Only agents whose declared service answered our last probe. An agent that declares none is excluded, not failed.

sort.description: One named dimension: independent, dealings, usd, completion, recent, paidBack, largestShare, counterparties, serving, suppliers, largestSupplierShare or spent. The last three order by what an agent rests on rather than by who rests on it. There is no "best" — nothing here has earned the right to rank.

spreadSuppliers.description: Only agents that PAY somebody and where no single party takes more than half of what the agent itself SPENDS. The other direction from the concentration of its custom: an agent with forty payers and one supplier looks diversified on every other figure here and is one supplier away from stopping. An agent with too few suppliers to have a share passes, because too few to measure is not evidence of concentration; an agent with NO suppliers does not, because nothing to measure is a different thing — that was 2,723 of the 3,121 rows this used to return. Use `supplierSpread=diversified` for the measured ones alone. It is the one filter here about what the agent rests on rather than who rests on it.

supplierSpread.description: The precise form of `spreadSuppliers`. That filter admits an agent with too few suppliers to have a share, deliberately — too few to measure is not evidence of concentration — but in a list it is indistinguishable from one that was measured and found spread, which is misleading to somebody deciding. Ask for `diversified` to get only the measured ones. `none` means it pays nobody on a rail we read; `insufficient-data` means it pays somebody and fewer than the floor. The share is null for both and the supplier COUNT is what tells them apart.

name: find_agents

answerLead.description: SINCE 2026-11-28: at most three lines before the full answer, from its own fields: `text`, `result`, `risks` (up to two), `asOf`, `coverage`, `unknowns` (up to two) and `deprecatedFields` (legacy duplicates this answer still carries). The full answer governs. Added by this MCP server; the REST route behind the tool does not carry it.

asOf.description: When the record behind these rows was last rebuilt. Null means nothing in the answer carries a date, which is a gap in our reading rather than a fact about the agents.

confirmedPaidEvidence.description: Where confirmedPaid was asked: the window (days, since), the rule, and how many addresses hold a confirmed-class event. Null where confirmedPaid was not asked. Each row carries its own `confirmedPaidEvidence` (rail, chain, txHash, logIndex, id, evidence, evidenceClass, at), null where not asked.

filters.description: What was applied, read back, including what a floor excluded.

identityMeans.description: SINCE 2026-11-27 (plugin audit P1-7): each row carries `identityLayers` {address, entity, service, operator, software, agent; each {state, basis}} (only the address is observed; entity, operator and software are never established; agent is protocol signals at most), `registryEvidence` [{registry erc8004 | acp | masumi | olas_mech | catalogue | endpoint_probe, level self_registered | protocol_recorded | third_party_listing | probe_response, state observed | none_observed | not_read, count, establishes, doesNotEstablish}] and `identitySays`. Each row’s `counterpartiesWithoutObservedPaymentBack` is the figure; `independent` is its deprecated alias.

items.description: Matching agents, ordered by the ONE dimension asked for, never a composite score. Each row carries `subject`: { type, evidence[], alsoShows[], says }. `evidence` names each thing we SAW and, in `supports`, which type it is evidence for — or null where the observation is real and separates nothing, which is the case for a catalogue listing. So `unknown` WITH evidence is the normal shape here and means "we saw these things and they do not settle it", never "we saw nothing". `alsoShows` carries the types a subject also shows evidence for, because they are not exclusive and dropping one would make the label more confident than the evidence. Measured once on 2026-10-11 and not refreshed since, over all 3,077 paid addresses: **1,377 agent, 38 marketplace, 1,662 unknown**. Those are a PAST reading kept because they are the point — this contract once claimed `unknown` would be commonest before anything had been measured, and the measurement found it at zero, which is how a defect in the classifier was caught. Read the answer’s own denominators for today’s mix; these say what KIND of mix to expect. A catalogue listing does NOT make a subject an API service. Agents sell priced endpoints too (this platform sells four), so a listing says it sells over HTTP and nothing about which kind of seller. `api-service` is therefore in the vocabulary and is currently UNREACHABLE: separating it would need evidence that a subject does NOT do agent work, and that is an absence, since 86% of these addresses pay nobody on a rail we read and paying from a second wallet looks identical to buying nothing.

meta.description: How current this answer is and what it was read from: `freshness` and the ages behind it. Present on every answer from this server, whatever the tool.

registrationIsNot.description: A registration is not proof of ownership or autonomy.

warnings.description: Anything the server wants a caller to know about THIS answer before acting on it, each {code, message, says} with message and says the same sentence. Empty is the normal case and is not a guarantee.

x402TiersAt.description: SINCE 2026-11-27 (plugin audit P0-1): when the x402 side of each row was split by evidence tier. On each row, settledPayers.x402ByTier and dealingsByKind.x402TransfersByTier are {known, total, confirmed_protocol, inferred_facilitator, candidate_catalogue, unknown}, summing to the figure they split; settledPayers.x402 and dealingsByKind.paymentsAndJobs are DEPRECATED aliases that count catalogue candidates as if settled. Null where the split has not been written: every split is then all unknown.
